finding.claim: big5 lead-byte recognizer accepts 0xFA-0xFE as lead bytes; a Buffer parameter containing FA 5C followed by a quote is emitted verbatim for the pair and the quote is escaped as 5C 27, so a server treating 0xFA as single-byte reads the 5C as an escape and the quote closes the literal (SQL injection). Medium confidence: server big5 lead range (0xA1-0xF9) recalled from memory, not verified.
finding.source: Buffer parameter bytes (e.g. FA 5C ' OR 1=1-- ) bound via ? in query() on a big5 connection (BIG5_CHINESE_CI or charset 'big5', lib/const/collations.js:57)
finding.sink: _BINARY '...' SQL literal sent to server (lib/cmd/query.js:120-122; lib/cmd/encoder/text-encoder.js:65-67)

trace.note: Buffer parameter routed to writeBufferEscape inside _BINARY literal
writeBufferEscapeMb used for big5 (mb recognizer registered)
isHead accepts 0xA1-0xFE, so 0xFA is treated as lead byte
valid pair FA 5C copied verbatim, no escape inserted before the 5C

finding.guards_checked: NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES mode uses quote doubling (packet-output-stream.js:689) so not affected; prepared statements / binary protocol build no SQL text so not affected; string path (writeDefaultStringEscapeQuote) escapes per char after iconv encoding so not affected; only the Buffer and stream-chunk path is affected.

finding.claim: For any server whose greeting claims MariaDB (version string contains 'MariaDB' or lacks CLIENT_MYSQL capability), strict TLS verification is silently disabled and the native-password scramble is sent before server identity is verified; the scramble allows offline password guessing. Native and ed25519 are misclassified as isMitmProof=true, so the self-signed guard does not block them. Flagged explicitly per org policy: weakens authentication and TLS verification.
finding.source: On-path attacker presenting an untrusted/self-signed cert with a MariaDB-looking greeting requesting mysql_native_password (or client_ed25519); app uses default strict TLS (ssl: true or rejectUnauthorized unset)
finding.sink: Password scramble sent over TLS to unauthenticated peer (lib/cmd/handshake/auth/handshake.js:134 via send at :77)

trace.note: mariaDb derived from attacker-controlled greeting (raw includes 'MariaDB' or CLIENT_MYSQL bit absent)
self-signed guard skipped because native isMitmProof is true
Handshake.send emits scramble before any identity check
identity/fingerprint check only at OK packet, after scramble already sent

finding.guards_checked: Auth-switch requireSecure (authentication.js:298) and clear-password guard (handshake.js:44) enforced; sha256, caching_sha2 and clear are blocked by handshake.js:67; constant-time fingerprint compare (authentication.js:243); non-MariaDB greetings protected because Node rejects untrusted cert; compensating fingerprint check runs only after scramble is sent.
